title: Matt Pocock's advice for security-critical TS apps: learn the type wizardry, use branded types
summary: A short essay arguing that TypeScript expertise, especially turning `any` into safe types and designing type-safe abstractions, saves teams bugs and speeds them up. For security-critical apps specifically, Matt says he'd lean heavily on branded types.

principles.text: Most TS app code is written under time pressure, which is how `any` creeps in.
principles.quote: The vast majority of TypeScript application code out there is written under severe time constraints.

principles.text: Knowing how to turn `any` into safe types saves your team bugs.
principles.quote: Having the knowledge to transform any’s into safe types will save your team bugs.

principles.text: Advanced type skills enable DX wins: custom forms, type-safe API endpoint creators, flexible components.
principles.quote: Want a custom form abstraction? A type-safe REST API endpoint creator? A flexible Table component?

principles.text: Enabling teammates to develop faster is what advances your career.
principles.quote: The more you can enable your teammates to develop faster, the faster you’ll rise up the ladder.

principles.text: For security-critical apps, use branded types extensively.
principles.quote: If I were building an app where security was critical, I’d use the crap out of branded types.

principles.text: Designing APIs that help others code faster is satisfying work.
principles.quote: You’ll be designing and implementing API’s that help folks code faster.
